records.gloss: For the director, on the gittith. Of [the] sons of Korah. A psalm.
pieces: For the music director. On the gittith. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

L.1: For the director: on the gittith. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

R.1: For the leader of the music. Set to "the Gittith". By the family of Korah. A song.

decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: the gittith: an instrument or tune, perhaps from Gath
decisions.reason: The word (gittit) is found in the titles of Psalms 8, 81 and 84. It may be an instrument or tune from the city of Gath, or be linked with the word for a winepress (gat). Its sense is no longer known.

decisions.choice: the sons of Korah: a family of Levite singers
decisions.reason: The descendants of Korah, a Levite (Numbers 26:11), served as gatekeepers and singers at the temple (1 Chronicles 9:19; 2 Chronicles 20:19). Eleven psalms carry their name (42-49, 84-85, 87-88). "Of" may mean the psalm belongs to their collection or was written by one of them.

records.heading: Longing for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house

records.gloss: How beloved [are] your dwellings, YHWH of hosts!
pieces: How deeply loved is {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} dwelling place, \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies!

R.2: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q the place where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} live is so dear to me!

decisions.reason: The psalm is the song of someone who longs for the temple in Jerusalem (verses 3-5) and makes the journey there (verses 6-8), like Psalms 42-43, also of the sons of Korah.
The word (yadid) means beloved, as Benjamin is "the beloved of the LORD" (Deuteronomy 33:12). The temple is loved because God lives there.
The plural (mishkenot) is often used for a single dwelling, as in 43:3 and 46:5.

The title (YHWH tseba'ot) names the LORD as commander of the armies of heaven, his angels and the stars (1 Kings 22:19; Isaiah 40:26), and of Israel's army (1 Samuel 17:45). Literal keeps the older "hosts"; Balanced and Readable say "Armies", as in Isaiah.
Readable names who loves the place, the psalmist, as verse 3 does.

records.source: נִכְסְפָ֬ה וְגַם־כָּלְתָ֨ה׀נַפְשִׁי֮ לְחַצְר֪וֹת יְה֫וָ֥ה לִבִּ֥י וּבְשָׂרִ֑י יְ֝רַנְּנ֗וּ אֶ֣ל אֵֽל־חָֽי׃
records.gloss: My soul has longed and also fainted for [the] courts of YHWH; my heart and my flesh shout for joy to [the] living God.
pieces: My whole being longs, even aches, for the courts of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q heart and body, \q I shout with joy to the living God.

L.3: My soul has longed and even fainted for the courts of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q my heart and my flesh \q shout for joy to the living God.

R.3: I want so much to be in the courtyards of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house that I feel weak. \q With all my heart and body I sing for joy to the God who lives.

decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) is the living self, with its desires (42:2-3).
Worshipers gathered in the open courtyards around the temple building; only priests went inside (65:5; 100:4).

decisions.choice: shout for joy to: cry out to
alternatives: cry out for the living God
decisions.reason: The verb (ranan) is usually a ringing shout of joy. With "to" it may also mean a loud cry of longing for God, as in 42:3.
God is alive and acts, unlike idols (42:3; Joshua 3:10).
As in the earlier psalms, Balanced and Readable render nefesh as the self.

records.source: גַּם־צִפּ֨וֹר׀מָ֪צְאָה בַ֡יִת וּדְר֤וֹר׀קֵ֥ן לָהּ֮ אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֪תָה אֶפְרֹ֫חֶ֥יהָ אֶֽת־מִ֭זְבְּחוֹתֶיךָ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת מַ֝לְכִּ֗י וֵאלֹהָֽי׃
records.gloss: Even [the] bird has found a house, and [the] swallow a nest for herself, where she has put her young: your altars, YHWH of hosts, my King and my God.
pieces: The sparrow, too, has found itself a home, and the swallow has a nest where it keeps its young, \q beside {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altars, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q my King and my God.

L.4: Even the bird has found a house, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she has put her young: \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altars, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q my King and my God.

R.4: Even little birds have found homes there. \q They make nests for their babies near {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altars, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q my King and my God.

decisions.reason: The first word (tsippor) is any small bird, often the sparrow; the second (deror) is probably the swallow (Proverbs 26:2).
The birds nest near the altars, in the temple courts. The words may also be the psalmist's cry: the birds have their homes, and I long for your altars.

decisions.choice: your altars: the two altars of the temple
decisions.reason: The temple had an altar for burnt offerings in the courtyard and an altar for incense inside.
As in 5:3, God is the psalmist's king.

The title (YHWH tseba'ot) names the LORD as commander of the armies of heaven, his angels and the stars (1 Kings 22:19; Isaiah 40:26), and of Israel's army (1 Samuel 17:45). Literal keeps the older "hosts"; Balanced and Readable say "Armies", as in Isaiah.

records.source: אַ֭שְׁרֵי יוֹשְׁבֵ֣י בֵיתֶ֑ךָ ע֝֗וֹד יְֽהַלְל֥וּךָ סֶּֽלָה׃
records.gloss: How blessed [are those who] dwell [in] your house; still they praise you. Selah.
pieces: How blessed are the ones who live in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house; \q they never stop praising {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Selah

L.5: How blessed [are those who] dwell [in] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house; \q they still praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Selah

R.5: Life is truly good for those who live in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house. \q They praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all the time. Selah

decisions.choice: those who dwell in your house: the temple servants
alternatives: all who worship at the temple
decisions.reason: Those who live in God's house are probably the priests and Levites who serve there day by day, or anyone who stays near God in worship (23:6; 27:4).
As in 1:1, the word ('ashre) describes a life that is truly good.
The word ('od) means "yet" or "still": their praise goes on.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.
Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.source: אַשְׁרֵ֣י אָ֭דָם עֽוֹז־ל֥וֹ בָ֑ךְ מְ֝סִלּ֗וֹת בִּלְבָבָֽם׃
records.gloss: How blessed [is the] person [whose] strength [is] in you, highways in their heart.
pieces: How blessed are people who find their strength in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} \q and fix their hearts on the pilgrim highways.

L.6: How blessed [is the] {{gender:person|man}} whose strength [is] in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q [with] highways in their heart.

R.6: Life is truly good for people who get their strength from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q They love to travel on the roads to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house.

decisions.reason: The word (mesillot) is a built-up road. Here it is most likely the roads pilgrims took up to Jerusalem for the feasts: their hearts are set on the journey.
The Hebrew begins with one person ("to him") and goes on with "their heart": anyone, and all, who make the journey.
Balanced and Readable use the plural for the generic person, as the Hebrew itself does in the second half of the verse.

decisions.choice: they love to travel on the roads to your house
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m1).

records.source: עֹבְרֵ֤י׀בְּעֵ֣מֶק הַ֭בָּכָא מַעְיָ֣ן יְשִׁית֑וּהוּ גַּם־בְּ֝רָכ֗וֹת יַעְטֶ֥ה מוֹרֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Passing through [the] valley of the Baca, a spring they make it; also blessings [the] early rain covers.
pieces: When they travel through the Baca Valley, they make it a land of springs; \q the early rain wraps it in blessings.

L.7: Passing through the valley of Baca, they make it a spring; \q the early rain also covers [it with] blessings.

R.7: On the road they pass through the Valley of Baca, and they turn it into a place where springs flow. \q The first rains cover it with blessings.

decisions.choice: Baca: a dry valley, or the valley of weeping
decisions.reason: Baca is not otherwise known as a place. The word names a kind of tree or shrub (2 Samuel 5) that grows in dry places, and it sounds like the word for weeping. Either way it is a hard stretch of the road, made a place of springs.

decisions.choice: blessings: the vowels as they stand
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew letters can be read "blessings" (berakhot) or "pools" (berekhot). The vowels of the Hebrew text give "blessings"; the rain covers the valley with good things.

decisions.choice: the early rain: the first autumn rain
decisions.reason: The first rains fell in October and November, after the dry summer, softening the ground for sowing (Deuteronomy 11:14).

records.source: יֵ֭לְכוּ מֵחַ֣יִל אֶל־חָ֑יִל יֵרָאֶ֖ה אֶל־אֱלֹהִ֣ים בְּצִיּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: They go from strength to strength; he appears before God in Zion.
pieces: They walk on from strength to strength, \q till every one of them comes before God in Zion.

L.8: They go from strength to strength; \q [each one] appears before God in Zion.

R.8: They get stronger and stronger as they go, \q until they all stand before God in Zion.

decisions.choice: from strength to strength: growing stronger
decisions.reason: Instead of tiring on the road, the pilgrims gain strength as they near Zion (Isaiah 40:31).

decisions.choice: appears before God: comes to the festival
decisions.reason: Every Israelite man was to appear before the LORD three times a year at the feasts (Exodus 23:17; Deuteronomy 16:16).

alternatives: the God of gods will be seen in Zion (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation read the same letters as "the God of gods will be seen in Zion". The Hebrew text as it stands says the pilgrim appears before God.

decisions.choice: every one of them (B); they all (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is singular: each one of the pilgrims.

records.source: יְה֘וָ֤ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים צְ֭בָאוֹת שִׁמְעָ֣ה תְפִלָּתִ֑י הַאֲזִ֨ינָה אֱלֹהֵ֖י יַעֲקֹ֣ב סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: YHWH God hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, God of Jacob! Selah.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies, hear my prayer; \q turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear to me, God of Jacob! Selah

L.9: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God of hosts, hear my prayer; \q give ear, God of Jacob! Selah

R.9: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies, listen as I pray. \q Hear me, God of Jacob's people! Selah

decisions.reason: The same chain of names as in 80:5.
As with "the LORD of hosts", the title names God as commander of the armies of heaven and of his people. Literal keeps the older "hosts"; Balanced and Readable say "Armies".

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.
Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.source: מָ֭גִנֵּנוּ רְאֵ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְ֝הַבֵּ֗ט פְּנֵ֣י מְשִׁיחֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Our shield see, God, and look at [the] face of your anointed.
pieces: God, see our shield; \q look with care on the face of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anointed one.

L.10: Our shield, see, God, \q and look at the face of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anointed.

R.10: God, look at the king who protects us like a shield. \q Be kind to the king {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have chosen.

alternatives: God, our shield, look (on your anointed)
decisions.reason: "Our shield" is most likely the king, named again in the second half as God's anointed (47:10; 89:19). It can also be read as a title for God: "see, God our shield".
The anointed one (mashiach) is the king of Israel, anointed with oil when he took the throne (2:2; 18:51). The pilgrims pray for him.

decisions.choice: look at the face: look with favor
decisions.reason: To look at someone's face is to give him a favorable hearing.

decisions.choice: the king who protects us like a shield; the king you have chosen
decisions.reason: Readable says who is meant (m1, m2).

records.source: כִּ֤י טֽוֹב־י֥וֹם בַּחֲצֵרֶ֗יךָ מֵ֫אָ֥לֶף בָּחַ֗רְתִּי הִ֭סְתּוֹפֵף בְּבֵ֣ית אֱלֹהַ֑י מִ֝דּ֗וּר בְּאָהֳלֵי־רֶֽשַׁע׃
records.gloss: For better [is] a day in your courts than a thousand; I have chosen standing at the threshold in [the] house of my God than dwelling in [the] tents of wickedness.
pieces: Truly, one day spent in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} courts is worth more than a thousand anywhere else; \q I would choose to stand at the threshold of my God's house \q over living in the tents of wicked people.

L.11: For better [is] a day in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} courts than a thousand; \q I have chosen to stand at the threshold in the house of my God \q rather than to dwell in [the] tents of wickedness.

R.11: Spending one day in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} courtyards is better than spending a thousand days somewhere else. \q I would rather stand at the door of my God's house \q than live in the homes of evil people.

decisions.choice: stand at the threshold: wait at the door
decisions.reason: The verb (histofef) is found only here and comes from the word for a threshold. It may mean to keep the door, as the sons of Korah did (1 Chronicles 9:19), or simply to stand at the entrance. Even the humblest place near God is better.

decisions.choice: than a thousand: a thousand days elsewhere
decisions.reason: "Days" is understood from the first half of the line.

decisions.choice: tents of wickedness: the homes of the wicked
decisions.reason: Tents stand for homes and households (83:7).
Balanced and Readable say where the thousand days are spent (m2).

records.source: כִּ֤י שֶׁ֨מֶשׁ׀וּמָגֵן֮ יְהוָ֪ה אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים חֵ֣ן וְ֭כָבוֹד יִתֵּ֣ן יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֥א יִמְנַע־ט֝֗וֹב לַֽהֹלְכִ֥ים בְּתָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: For a sun and a shield [is] YHWH God; favor and honor gives YHWH; not he withholds good from [those who] walk in blamelessness.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God is both sun and shield; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives favor and honor; \q from those who walk blamelessly {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keeps back nothing good.

L.12: For a sun and a shield [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God; \q favor and honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not withhold good from those who walk in blamelessness.

R.12: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God gives light like the sun and protects like a shield. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} shows kindness and gives honor. \q He does not hold back anything good from people who live without blame.

decisions.choice: a sun: the giver of light and life
decisions.reason: Only here is God called a sun. The sun gives light and warmth and makes things grow; the shield protects (3:4).

decisions.choice: a sun and a shield: the Hebrew text
alternatives: the LORD loves mercy and truth (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation has "for the LORD God loves mercy and truth" here. The Hebrew text has "sun and shield".
The first word (chen) is kindness shown freely; the second (kavod) is honor or glory, the weight and standing God gives.

decisions.choice: blamelessness: a whole and honest life
decisions.reason: The word (tamim) means complete, without fault (15:2; 18:24).

decisions.choice: gives light like the sun and protects like a shield
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pictures mean (m1).

records.source: יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֑וֹת אַֽשְׁרֵ֥י אָ֝דָ֗ם בֹּטֵ֥חַ בָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: YHWH of hosts, how blessed [is the] person [who] trusts in you!
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q how blessed is anyone who trusts in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!

L.13: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q how blessed [is the] {{gender:person|man}} [who] trusts in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!

R.13: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q life is truly good for anyone who trusts in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!

decisions.reason: As in verses 5 and 6, the third "how blessed" of the psalm.
The word ('adam) means a human being, man or woman.

The title (YHWH tseba'ot) names the LORD as commander of the armies of heaven, his angels and the stars (1 Kings 22:19; Isaiah 40:26), and of Israel's army (1 Samuel 17:45). Literal keeps the older "hosts"; Balanced and Readable say "Armies", as in Isaiah.
